gaps.wanted: The top, the bottom and the right wall. The guide's figures show the lid plain and no underside. Figure 1-12 (PDF p36, printed 1-12) shows the right wall only in part, behind the rack bracket. No held picture shows the part it hides. The right wall is left as a later part of its own.
The stretch of the left wall between 137 and 268 mm from the rear. The photographed switches are 299 mm deep. No held picture shows a 386 mm model's wall, so the stretch is drawn plain.

The RPS connector is the part cisco/rps2300-connector@2, drawn open where the photograph puts it. The part draws the plate, its two screw holes, the shroud with its dark top edge, the housing and the two rows of eleven cavities with a contact in each; it draws the cells with their chamfered lower corners and does not draw the slot in the screws, which the photograph shows at about one pixel. The rating strip stays chassis art. The guide says the cover (two Phillips pan-head screws, Figure 1-15) goes on when no RPS is connected.

This model's own rear in colour. The only held rear in colour with the FlexStack slot is the NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-48LPD-L, whose plain plate reads #3f4447 (median of 2000 px, box (440,15,520,40)) and whose fitted module's plain frame reads #3f565d; its printed ratings ("8-4A", "+12V @11.25A, -48V @7.8A") match none of the five rows of spec Tables 1-2 and 1-3, so it is another model's rear. The NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-24TS-L rear (1102 x 97 px, a model with no FlexStack slot, used only as a cross-check and never drawn from) reads #404145 (1120 px, box (520,8,590,24)) and #44464a (1800 px, box (880,30,940,60)): the two photographs agree to within 5 levels of 255 in each channel. The drawn #404040 is 1 level above, 4 below and 7 below the 48LPD-L median in red, green and blue, so it is a stand-in within a few levels of the photographs and is kept. The guide's own drawing of the rear (Figure 1-10, PDF p19, printed 1-17) is pale grey: its rear face reads #d4d6d8 (3500 px, box (330,150,430,185) of the converted figure), its top face #bebdbb (15000 px, box (400,50,700,100)) and its side face #8f908f (1250 px, box (940,215,990,240)), three different greys, so the figure shades one pale finish by the light on each face and does not draw the rear charcoal. The guide gives no housing colour and says nothing of a shared finish ("All the 24- and 48-port switches have similar components" is about parts). The rear is drawn in the chassis colour, #404040, which is the front's own measured panel colour: a stand-in, in conflict with Figure 1-10, that the owner may accept or replace.

The ETSI mounting bracket, printed "700-19781XX" (PDF p34, printed 1-10). Its revision digits are not read, and the guide gives no contents or install steps beyond Figure 1-10, so no kit contract is written.

Three things on the NetBox stencil are not drawn; the USB symbol is, from the stencil, as white strokes and discs 2.8 x 5.2 mm (#ffffff, 25 px, box (4497,93,4502,98)). The Cisco logo is never drawn (the region `logo-zone` stays). The "740 W" after "POWER over ETHERNET" under the first jack block reads on the stencil at 10x as the digits 7, 4, 0 and a W, but it is printed black on the dark panel and across the yellow ticks (contrast about 2 to 1), so it cannot be read at the page's scale on either stage and is not drawn. The guide prints "740 W" only as the PoE budget (Table 1-1, PDF p4, printed 1-2) and in Table 1-2 (PDF p62, printed 1-2), never as a mark on the front. The corner marks (16 of them: 1X, 11X, 2X, 12X; 13X, 23X, 14X, 24X; 25X, 35X, 26X, 36X; 37X, 47X, 38X and 48X, at the corners of the four blocks, cap height 1.23 mm) read clearly on the stencil, but "corner marks 1X to 48X" sit where the jack part's box begins: each mark's inner 0.6 to 1.0 mm lies under the part, and a silkscreen line lies under the parts, so a mark would be half hidden and is not drawn. The strip's "POWER over ETHERNET" and the yellow ticks are drawn from the stencil. The ticks are a motif whose gaps take the renderer's own dark (#17191c), a shade under the panel's #404040.
A square-on photograph of this model's front. The only flat face is community art; every position is read from it at 11.3 px per mm.
The Mode button is drawn as plain panel art. No library part is a flush push button of this shape.

Label figures are another model's, kept as stand-ins. This model's own rear label text is not held. The rear labels (the warning above the RPS plate, the ratings line over its pins and the rating plate beside the inlet) are drawn as the NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-48LPD-L rear prints them, and that photograph is another model's rear: its figures are stand-ins, every one `estimated`. It prints "8-4A, 50-60Hz" and "+12V ... @11.25A, -48V ... @7.8A", which match none of the five models' rows of the guide's tables, and the guide's own drawings of the rear (Figure 1-10, PDF p19, printed 1-17, and Figure 1-13, PDF p21, printed 1-19) print "12-6A", so the guide's drawing is not followed either. What each model's own label should read, from its own row of Table 1-2 (PDF p62, printed 1-2) and Table 1-3 (PDF p64, printed 1-4): the WS-C2960S-48FPD-L, AC 9 to 4 A and +12 V @ 4 A, -52 V @ 15 A; the 48LPD-L, 5 to 2 A and +12 V @ 4 A, -52 V @ 8 A; the 24PD-L, 5 to 2 A and +12 V @ 3 A, -52 V @ 8 A; the 48TD-L, 1 to 0.5 A and +12 V @ 4 A; the 24TD-L, 1 to 0.5 A and +12 V @ 3 A. All five: 100 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz. Which figures the label should show is the owner's decision: keep the photograph's as stand-ins, or show this model's own row.

A version of the SFP+ cage part with the stencil's silver frame (#cfcfcf, 1423 px of each cage), its two clips on the right side (#bdbdbd with black edges), its two small squares near the top (#707070), its gold contacts at the lower left and its pull tab inside the opening. The part's own skin paints a grey collar (#9aa0a8) round a dark opening and its skin is not edited here. Drawn outside or under the part's box: the silver as the surround the part leaves visible (about 0.5 mm each side), the black projection at each cage's foot (#000000, 861 px, box (4570,427,4652,441)), the silver pull tab (#c1c5cb, 240 px, box (4588,416,4636,421); all but about 0.2 mm of it lies under the part's box and is hidden) and the white numeral tab under each cage (#f2f2f2, 2112 px, box (4570,450,4652,477)) with its numeral in #595959 (70 px, box (4600,456,4624,474)). Not drawn: the clips, the squares and the gold contacts, because they lie inside the cage's own opening and would paint over the part's skin. Request: `std/sfp` with the clips, squares, contacts and pull tab in its opening.

A `common/led-arrow-sm` skin whose off fill is the stencil's solid light grey (#808080: 120 px, box (520,96,535,104) of a port arrow and 155 px, box (4660,118,4676,128) of the console arrow; each arrow 2.38 x 2.12 mm) without the dark fill and the #5b6167 edge. The part is on `main` and its skin is not edited, and a lamp's colour in the static drawing is the part's own (a lamp state paints only when a state is set), so each lamp keeps its dark triangle; a light grey triangle of the stencil's size is drawn under it, which leaves a light rim of about 0.25 mm, and the black disc the punched lamp opening drew is covered in the panel's colour. The three lamps by the console and management jacks are arrows too (Figure 1-9, PDF p18, printed 1-16, "Console LEDs": 1 USB console LED, 2 RJ-45 console LED; Table 1-10 gives their colours): they were round dots and are arrow lamps now, down for the USB console LED, right for the RJ-45 console LED (the up skin turned 90 degrees: a lamp, not a connector) and up under the management jack.

A white or silver body for the RJ-45 part. The console jack, the management jack and the 48 jack-block jacks are `std/rj45-ganged@2`, whose only skin paints a near-black body with light grey shoulders. The stencil draws the console and management jacks on a white plate (#efefef, 10086 px of each, boxes (4782,86,4959,226) and (4998,86,5175,226)) round a dark opening, so a plate of that colour and outline (15.6 x 12.34 mm) is drawn under each of the two jacks and the part keeps its own body. On the 48 block jacks the stencil draws charcoal bodies with white shoulders, where the render has near-black bodies with light grey shoulders; left: the part's skin. Request: an `std/rj45` skin with a white body or white shoulders. The latch stays up and the contacts down, as the stencil shows them.

A USB-A skin with a silver interior and the tongue at the left, as the stencil shows. `std/usb-a@1` is placed with `skin: usb2` and rotated 90 degrees, and draws a black opening (#17191c) with a pale tongue (#d5d9de) to the right of the middle of the vertical opening; the stencil draws a silver-grey shell with the tongue at the left. Neither skin of the part draws a silver interior (`default` draws a blue tongue, `usb2` a white one, in the same place), so the part stays as it is. The only way to bring the tongue to the left with this skin is a 270 degree turn of the placed part, which is a rotation and is the owner's to decide. Figure 1-1 (PDF p4, printed 1-2) is too small at this port to say more. The shell around the part is drawn silver (#7b7b7b).

A mini-B skin with the five contacts in the lower half of the opening. `std/mini-usb@1` draws the flat edge at the top, bevelled corners at the bottom and the five contacts (#7a8087) in the upper half; the stencil has the same flat edge and bevel and the contacts in the lower half. The stencil is the only source of the contact side: Figure 1-5 (USB Mini-Type B Port, PDF p9, printed 1-7) draws a mini-B port with the bevelled corners at the top and contacts both on its tongue and in a row below it, which does not settle the side for this connector as it is mounted, and Figure 1-1 (PDF p4, printed 1-2) is too small. The part's skin is not edited and the connector is not turned: turning it would put the bevel on top, and a rotation after merge is a major version.

The "MGMT" and "BASET" legend right of the management jack. The stencil prints it vertically in yellow (#ffff99, 341 px, box (5190,95,5215,212)): the letters M, G, M, T, then a gap, then B, A, S, E, T, one above the other and upright, each 0.78 mm tall, 10.3 mm in all (it reads "BASET", with no hyphen, at 6x). A legend 0.78 mm tall is under the 1.5 mm font size the library's legend test asks for, so it is not drawn. Wanted: a photograph or a dimensioned front that gives the legend at a size that reads.

The photograph shows the three pins of the AC inlet as dark pockets, each with a small light mark. It also shows two curved light lines inside the inlet's foot. The render draws light grey pin blocks. The inlet is std/c14-inlet@1, which many parts place, so a new version of that part draws the pins, not this device. The pin pockets are left as a later part of their own.
the buried marks moved clear of the components that paint over them

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

an `attrs.performance` section; `cpu`, `memory` in a missing `attrs.platform` section; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power`; one of `operating-temp`, `operating-temp-f2b`, `operating-temp-b2f` in a missing `attrs.environmental` section (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 1 bay (rear 1); `physical-context` on port groups rj45, sfp-plus - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

airflow.note: The guide names a fan exhaust on the rear panel and counts no fans and gives no direction; no airflow is set and no fan redundancy is claimed. The exhaust is drawn where Figure 1-10 and the photograph put it.

colour.note: Front: the faceplate is two-tone, read from the NetBox WS-C2960S-48FPD-L stencil (cisco-ws-c2960s-48fpd-l.front.png, 5475 x 503 px), whose fills are flat. The largest plain area is the charcoal panel, #404040 (median of 3600 px, box (435,30,480,110)), so that is `chassis.color`. The teal bezel round it is #255e6d (median of 7000 px, box (700,6,1200,20); the same on the lower edge, box (700,482,1200,497)); the console surround is #bad4d7 and the jack-block, SFP+ cage and management-jack outlines and the port-number tags are #ffff99. Lamp and model legends are inked as the stencil prints them: #ffffff for the lamps, #bbd5d8 for CONSOLE and #f2f2f2 for the model name. A NetBox stencil is a community artist's flat render, so these are that artist's palette and not a reading of the metal. Figure 1-1 (PDF p4, printed 1-2), Cisco's own colour drawing of this model, agrees on the scheme (a dark teal front edge round a charcoal panel, yellow frames round the jack blocks, a pale-grey lid) with its own fills: panel #4a5153, teal #1d5e7a, yellow #fff647, lid #c3c4c7 (exact pixel colours of the figure's vector fills, 400 dpi render of the page). Those are within 10 to 20 of 255 of the stencil's and are not used; the stencil is kept because the other models' stencils give the same set. The stencil of this model draws the jack-block outlines white (#ffffff) and those of the SFP+ cages and management jack yellow (#ffff99); Figure 1-1 of this model draws all of them yellow, and the 48TD-L stencil draws the blocks yellow too, so the blocks are drawn yellow here and the white is the stencil artist's choice. Rear: no held rear carries this model's colour. The only rear in colour is the WS-C2960S-48LPD-L NetBox photograph, whose plain rear plate reads #3f4447 (median of 2000 px, box (440,15,520,40)) and whose fitted module's plain frame reads #3f565d (500 px, box (230,137,330,142)); a photograph's colour depends on its lighting. Its printed ratings (AC "8-4A", RPS "+12V @11.25A, -48V @7.8A") match none of the five rows of spec Tables 1-2 and 1-3, so it is not proof of the 48LPD-L's own rear. The guide names no housing colour and says nothing of a shared finish. The rear is therefore drawn in the chassis colour and the `faceplate-colour` gap says so. The rear reads charcoal, not teal; the teal is the fitted module's frame only. The lid and sides, which Figure 1-1 draws grey, stay `empty:`.

console.note: Figure 1-1 callouts 5 and 6 and "Management Ports" (Figure 1-5, PDF p9): the USB mini-Type B console port and the RJ-45 console port are one console, and the USB port has priority when both are cabled (Table 1-10). The management port is its own (callout 7).

controls-and-lamps.note: The eight switch lamps (SYST, RPS, MSTR, STAT, DPLX, SPED, STCK, PoE) stand in a column at 7.1 mm, pitched 2.53 mm, the Mode button below them (Figure 1-7, PDF p13, printed 1-11: System, RPS, Master, Status, Duplex, Speed, Stack, PoE, Mode button; the RPS lamp is "only on switch models that support RPS", the Master and Stack lamps "only on switch models that support stacking", the PoE lamp "only on switch models that support PoE"). The two small arrows above each column pair are the port lamps; the stencil shows them as triangles, up for the upper port and down for the lower, so the library's up and down arrow skins are used. The port lamp's meaning depends on the selected mode (Table 1-9). The arrows by the console jacks are the USB and RJ-45 console lamps (Figure 1-9 and Table 1-10, PDF p18, printed 1-16: "Console LEDs"), a down arrow and a right arrow beside CONSOLE, and the arrow under the management jack is its lamp (Table 1-11, PDF p19, printed 1-17); all three are arrow lamps, as the stencil and Figure 1-9 draw them.

ears-and-kits.note: Figure 1-12 (PDF p36, printed 1-12) "Attaching Brackets for 19-inch Racks": front-mounting, mid-mounting and rear-mounting positions, with number-8 Phillips flat-head screws (48-0655-01); Figure 1-13 (PDF p37, printed 1-13): number-12 Phillips pan-head screws (48-0523-01) for the rack and a black Phillips machine screw (48-0654-01) for the cable guide. The text says four screws attach each bracket's long side to the switch. The 19-inch brackets are in the box, so they are not a kit. No position is dimensioned, so none carries an `at`. The ETSI bracket is printed "700-19781XX" (PDF p34, printed 1-10), with its revision digits unread: it is a gap and not a kit.

front-console-end.note: The shapes at the console end are read from the NetBox front elevations of the WS-C2960S-48FPD-L, -48TD-L, -24PD-L and -24TD-L (cisco-ws-c2960s-<model>-l.front.png, 5475 x 503 px, 11.345 px per mm, the chassis starting 216 px in, so one pixel is 0.09 mm). The four agree on every shape here. A model whose own stencil is another product is read from them. The legend band's left end slopes from (384.2, 2.1) to (394.5, 4.6) mm: the first teal pixel of each row runs from 4584 to 4683 px over rows 26 to 50. The dark panel's top-right corner is rounded at about 2.2 mm: the teal ends at 5191 px in row 53 and at 5213 px from row 77. The console surround stops at 24.42 mm under the mini-B jack and at 21.24 mm under the RJ-45 jack, with the step at 402.1 mm, so the surround and its dark panel are two rectangles each, and the port lamp below stands on the panel. The stencil rounds the inside of the step by about 0.9 mm and it is drawn square here. The mini-B's lower corners show the surround's teal in the stencil, so two teal triangles, 0.8 by 1.2 mm, cover the hole's black beside the part's bevels.

front-marks.note: The arrows, the console label, the jack plates, the SFP+ tabs, the PoE tags and the USB symbol are read from the NetBox WS-C2960S-48FPD-L stencil (cisco-ws-c2960s-48fpd-l.front.png) at 11.345 px per mm, the chassis starting 216 px in, each colour the median of the plain pixels of its box; the stencil is a community artist's palette and no photograph from Cisco of the front is held, and a photograph's colours would depend on its lighting. Arrows: light grey #808080 (120 px, box (520,96,535,104), a port arrow; 155 px, box (4660,118,4676,128), the console arrow), each 2.38 x 2.12 mm, no circle; the lamps already stand within 0.2 mm of the stencil's arrows, so none moves, except the management lamp, 1.3 mm left of the jack's centre on the stencil, which does. The stencil's lamp-by-lamp order is up above odd ports and down above even ones, down under the USB-A and under the console surround, a down and a right arrow beside CONSOLE and an up arrow under the management jack. The console label CONSOLE is #bbd5d8 (578 px, box (4648,85,4746,101)), one level from the surround's #bad4d7, cap height 1.23 mm from baseline 8.81 mm, centred at 395.02 mm, inside the surround. The two jack plates are #efefef (10086 px each), 15.6 x 12.34 mm at (402.47, 7.58) and (421.51, 7.58) mm. Each SFP+ numeral tab is #f2f2f2 (2112 px, box (4570,450,4652,477)), 7.49 x 2.73 mm at (383.61, 39.49) and (413.75, 39.49) mm, its numeral #595959 (70 px, box (4600,456,4624,474)) 1.5 mm tall; the pull tab #c1c5cb (240 px, box (4588,416,4636,421)) and its black projection #000000 (861 px, box (4570,427,4652,441)). The PoE tags are 24, one for each pair of ports, 13.18 x 3.44 mm at y 2.64 mm, #ffff99 (240 px, box (490,32,530,38), the same as the earlier strip's value), measured by the runs of yellow along one pixel row: 23.89, 37.81, 51.74, 65.76, 79.68 and 93.61 mm in the first block and the same pitch in the other three. Figure 1-1 (PDF p4, printed 1-2) read at 4x also draws separate yellow tags, one for each pair, above the lamps, and a yellow bar at the end of each block; the earlier note that it draws one bar for each block of twelve was wrong. The USB symbol is white (#ffffff, 25 px, box (4497,93,4502,98)), 2.8 x 5.2 mm, drawn as strokes and discs. Figure 1-9 (PDF p18, printed 1-16) shows the same arrows beside CONSOLE and under the jacks and calls the first two the console LEDs.

front-plates.note: Read from the NetBox WS-C2960S-48FPD-L stencil (cisco-ws-c2960s-48fpd-l.front.png) at 11.345 px per mm, the chassis starting 216 px in; the 48TD-L and 24PD-L stencils give the same value for every figure here. Each block of twelve sits in a ring (#ffffff on this model, 1800 px, box (450,200,460,380); yellow on the other stencils), round a dark channel and a silver plate (#efefef, the pixels of 0xd0 or more outside the bar, 23316 px, box (473,146,1443,260)) with a silver bar between the two rows (#dcdcdc, 31850 px, box (503,264,1413,299)). The MODE button is teal #255e6d (1375 px, box (330,435,385,460)) in a black rim #020404 (90 px, box (315,430,318,460)), 85 x 62 px, 7.5 x 5.46 mm. It was already declared teal and read as a dark tab because the bezel beside it is the same teal: it had no rim. The USB-A shell is #7b7b7b (7675 px, box (4541,80,4595,228)) and the two SFP+ frames #cfcfcf (1423 px, box (4526,310,4697,444) and 1424 px, box (4866,310,5037,444)). The ticks are 47 to a block, 0.44 mm wide on a 1.799 mm pitch from 481 px, #ffff99 (110 px, box (481,446,486,468)). All medians. The ring is white on this stencil and Figure 1-1 (PDF p4, printed 1-2) draws the frames yellow, so the yellow outline stays round the white ring: the figure is isometric and too small to tell a ring from a frame. The stencil is a community artist's flat render, so these are that artist's palette; no photograph from Cisco of the front is held.

gate-1-front.note: The front is read from the NetBox front elevation of the WS-C2960S-48FPD-L, checked against the guide first. Its aspect is 5475 / 503 = 10.88 against 482.6 / 44.45 = 10.86 for the 19-inch width the ears make, so the image runs ear tip to ear tip and is read at 11.345 px per mm, with the chassis starting 216 px (19.05 mm) in. The 48 jacks agree with Table 1-1, four blocks of twelve in two rows, and the USB Type A, mini-B, RJ-45 console, management and two SFP+ slots agree with Figure 1-1 callouts 3 to 7. The jack pitch reads 13.96 mm across 24 columns against the 13.97 of std/rj45-ganged, which supports the scale; the drawn chassis is 441 mm between its ears' edges, 0.8 % under the stated 444.5, so every position is `estimated`. The NetBox image is community art, not Cisco's.

inlet.note: The inlet is an IEC C14 appliance inlet, read from Figures 1-10 and 1-11 (a three-pin keyed inlet with a rating label beside it) and the NetBox 48LPD-L rear photograph. The guide does not name the connector type; it says "Use the supplied AC power cord" and describes an optional power cord retainer (PWR-CLP=, PDF p42, printed 1-18). Position is read from the NetBox 48LPD-L rear photograph (same stacking rear, Figure 1-10; 3.41 px per mm from the 444.5 mm width, 1516 px).

jacks.note: Row 1 starts 11.72 mm down the face and row 2 at 26.71, 15.0 apart; the first block's first jack at 24.06 mm from the chassis side and the blocks 89.4 mm apart (6 x 13.97 plus a 5.58 gutter). Jack height 11.0 reads 11.0 on the elevation. Upper-row jacks are drawn with their contacts at the bottom of the opening, so they take the 180-degree rotation the 4948E's upper row takes.

legend.note: The legend "Catalyst 2960-S Series PoE+ 10G" is printed on the NetBox stencil's face. Figure 1-1 shows only "2960-S" under the console callout, so the full text is the stencil's, which is community art, not this model's own document; it is carried as `estimated`.

lifecycle.note: No lifecycle date is carried. The end-of-sale notices are not held; only titles and list dates would be, and this model's is not among them.

numbering.note: Ports run left to right from the far left, port 1 above port 2 in each pair, and the module slots are 49 and 50 (the note under Figure 1-3, PDF p5, printed 1-3). The elevation prints 1 and 2 over each column pair, 1X and 2X at the first column's corners. The numerals are carried on the face as printed on the strip above the jacks. Interface names are in the community NetBox device type only: GigabitEthernet1/0/1 to 1/0/48, TenGigabitEthernet1/0/1 and 1/0/2 for the two slots and FastEthernet0 for the management port.

power.note: Spec Table 1-2, this model's row: AC input 100 to 240 VAC autoranging, 9 to 4 A, 50 to 60 Hz; DC input for the RPS 2300 +12 V @ 4 A and -52 V @ 15 A; power consumption 129 W, 440 BTUs per hour (footnote 1: the power consumed internally by the switch at 120 VAC, 60 Hz); power rating 0.89 KVA. The PoE budget is 740 W (Table 1-1). The supply is built in: "The switch is powered through the internal power supply" (AC Power Connector, PDF p21-22, printed 1-19 to 1-20), so it is part of the chassis and not a bay.

rear.note: The rear is the stacking models' common rear (Figure 1-10, with the RPS connector: callouts 1 FlexStack module slot and cover, 2 fan exhaust, 3 RPS connector, 4 AC power connector). The guide's figure is isometric, so positions come from the NetBox 48LPD-L rear photograph, a different model of the same rear, read at 3.41 px per mm along its width. It shows a C2960S-STACK module fitted; this device shows the blank cover (the module is optional: "FlexStack Ports", PDF p21, printed 1-19). Spec Table 1-2 lists a DC input for the RPS 2300 for this model, so the RPS connector is present. The guide says "If you are not using an RPS with your switch, use the two Phillips pan-head screws to attach the RPS connector cover" (Figure 1-15, PDF p39, printed 1-15), so the connector is drawn open, as the photograph shows it. It is the part cisco/rps2300-connector@2 (interface `cisco-rps2300`), seated at the plate's place; the rating strip stays chassis art. Measured on the photograph at 3.41 px per mm: a metal plate 72.8 x 22.6 mm at (285.0, 21.4) with a raised rating strip above it (49.2 x 3.8 mm at 297.7, 17.9), a black shroud 48.2 x 11.3 mm at (298.4, 24.0) holding a cream housing 46.9 x 9.7 mm, and in it two rows of eleven cavities, 3.5 x 3.7 mm each, on a 4.17 mm pitch across and 4.03 mm between the rows, with a screw hole at each end of the plate (centres 294.7 and 350.2 mm, 29.8 mm down). Eleven across is what the serial-number figures draw for the PoE and the TD models (PDF p55, printed 1-5, Figure 1-1 of the appendix, and PDF p56, printed 1-6, Figure 1-2); Figure 1-10 (PDF p19, printed 1-17) draws seven across in a smaller figure, and the photograph and the two larger figures are followed. The warning label above the plate ("DC inputs for remote power supply specified in manual", with a triangle) is printed on the metal at (294.0, 5.9), 45.2 x 9.7 mm; its triangle and three lines, the ratings line over the pins and the rating plate beside the inlet (32.7 x 13.4 mm at (351.0, 6.1)) are drawn as the photograph prints them, which is another model's text and is declared a stand-in (see `rear-labels` and the gap `rear-label-text`). The inlet sits in a moulded black surround 29.3 x 22.5 mm at (387.6, 8.3). The fan exhaust is a honeycomb of hexagons about 9.7 x 8.5 mm on an 8.8 mm column pitch, centres measured from the dark cells of the photograph (21 cells, flat-topped); the library's `vent` pattern is hexagonal and is the nearest of the schema's patterns, scaled by 2.0 with `pattern-pitch` to that pitch, and its tile is crisp (a filled hexagon, no stroke and no filter), so `motif` is not needed. The faintness in the earlier comparison was the cairosvg rasteriser, which resamples a scaled pattern tile; in Chromium, the viewer's own rasteriser, the holes are sharp. The three screws along the rear carry the cross the module's own screws use (see `rear-colours`). The web between the holes is the chassis colour, not bright metal: the photograph's web reads #404345 (3999 px of the pixels between 40 and 130, box (540,44,705,140)) against the plate's #3f4447, and the holes #040507 (256 px, box (572,52,588,68)); only the cut edges above and below the field are light, #b9bcba (517 px, box (533,40,712,46)), drawn as two thin strips. The renderer's `vent` and `motif` tiles both fill their holes #17191c, so the holes are a shade lighter than the photograph's. The web is a plate under the field. Four pan-head screws, 6.8 mm across, stand at 7.3, 111.4, 274.2 and 436.4 mm along and 28.7 mm down; the first is on the module's flange and is drawn with the cover. The FlexStack slot is the fitted module's stepped frame (see the blank cover's contract). The stamped corner marks round the fan and the small drilled hole at (149.0, 28.9) are drawn (see `rear-details`).

side-left.note: The left wall's 29 openings (17 peanut slots, 7 round holes, 5 small rectangles) are placed from photographs of the product. The photographs show two 299 mm models, a 24-port and a 48-port. Each opening is placed in millimetres from the rear and top edges, good to about 4 mm along and 2 mm across. The two photographs differ by at most 3.5 mm along the wall and 1.3 mm across it. Figure 1-10 (PDF p19, printed 1-17) gives the pattern: the count and kind of each opening. Figure 1-10 is captioned "Catalyst 2960-S Switch Rear Panel with Stacking Module Slot and RPS connector". It is a perspective view, so it gives the pattern but not the positions along the wall. The scale along the wall comes from each photographed model's own length, 299 mm (Table 1-3, PDF p65). This model is 386 mm deep (Table 1-2, PDF p63). The scale across the wall comes from the printed 44.45 mm height. Sizes along the wall come from the photographs too. In the figure, the rear group's slots and bars read about 1.4 times too long along the wall. No photograph of a 386 mm model's wall is held. Assumed: each group keeps its distance from its own end, leaving a plain stretch 87 mm longer than on the 299 mm models. Its four callouts do not name the openings: the figure shows 29 openings; the guide does not say what they are for. They stay drawn as marks. The openings' colour, #141414, is a stand-in dark; the figure's grey is shading. The wall keeps the device's colour. Figure 1-10 shows each of the 17 slots with a waist. The drawn outlines have none; the waists are a later part of their own.
